section_summary: This section documents State Department and Army handling of permits, visas, and occupation clearances for foreign nationals seeking to enter or leave Japan, including business travelers, missionaries, dependents, and company representatives. Individual cases involve permit renewals, cancellations, returned permits, delayed applications, and requests for additional information. The section also develops a broader procedure encouraging governments without missions in Japan to submit applications through their designated protecting powers.

subfiles.title: Letter returning Archibald S. R. Williamson’s military permit
subfiles.from: Walter F. Chappell, Division of Protective Services
subfiles.to: Lieutenant Colonel J. D. Scott, Military Permit Section
subfiles.about: Returns Williamson’s permit after notifying the American Embassy at Manila of his theater clearance.
subfiles.summary: Chappell returns Archibald S. R. Williamson’s military permit to the Army as Captain Rawls requested.

subfiles.title: Letter concerning renewed permits for Fathers Ponzelet and Thoneick
subfiles.from: Walter F. Chappell, Department of State
subfiles.to: H. J. Patzelt, Divine Word Missionaries
subfiles.about: Explains that the priests’ expired Japan permits are being reissued and requests their departure details.
subfiles.summary: The Army has been asked to reissue the priests’ expired permits; Patzelt should advise how to deliver them and provide departure details.

subfiles.title: Letter requesting new permits for Ponzelet and Thoneick
subfiles.from: Walter F. Chappell, Division of Protective Services
subfiles.to: Lieutenant Colonel J. D. Scott, Military Permit Section
subfiles.about: Requests replacement permits if theater clearance is renewed and returns Patzelt’s correspondence.
subfiles.summary: Chappell asks the Army to issue new permits for the two priests and encloses Patzelt’s letter and the Department’s reply.

subfiles.title: Army memorandum forwarding Patzelt’s letter
subfiles.from: Military Permit Section, Department of the Army
subfiles.to: Division of Protective Services, Department of State
subfiles.about: Forwards Patzelt’s request concerning travel by Ponzelet and Thoneick.
subfiles.summary: The Army asks State to act on Patzelt’s enclosed letter and return it when finished.

subfiles.title: Patzelt letter requesting reentry permits for two priests
subfiles.from: H. J. Patzelt, Divine Word Missionaries
subfiles.to: War Department, Division of Protective Services
subfiles.about: Asks whether Ponzelet and Thoneick must appear personally for permits before their March sailing.
subfiles.summary: Patzelt explains the priests’ Rome travel and asks whether their Japan reentry permits can be mailed before their scheduled March 13 departure.

subfiles.title: Memorandum for the files on Ponzelet and Thoneick
subfiles.from: Division of Protective Services
subfiles.about: Records calls establishing that the priests’ earlier permits expired and require reissuance.
subfiles.summary: Spence learned that both permits expired January 16 and arranged to send them to the Army for reissuance.

subfiles.title: Draft airgram authorizing Rosemary Muldoon’s travel
subfiles.from: Department of State
subfiles.about: Reports Muldoon’s clearance as John Muldoon’s dependent and explains transit and exit-permit procedures.
subfiles.summary: The Legation may document Rosemary Muldoon’s clearance for commercial travel to Japan and should explain U.S. transit and exit-permit requirements.

subfiles.title: Army clearance memorandum for Rosemary Muldoon
subfiles.from: Military Permit Section, Department of the Army
subfiles.about: Reports theater clearance for Rosemary Muldoon as a dependent traveling at private expense.
subfiles.summary: The Army reports Muldoon’s clearance for travel after April 1 and supplies her Dublin address.

subfiles.title: Army memorandum cancelling Karalis’s clearance
subfiles.from: Military Permit Section, Department of the Army
subfiles.about: Requests withdrawal and return of A. Karalis’s Japan entry permit.
subfiles.summary: The Army reports that Karalis’s clearance was cancelled and asks State to recover his permit.

subfiles.title: Telephone memorandum on Karalis and Gallaher
subfiles.from: H. C. Corkran, Division of Protective Services
subfiles.about: Records the Army’s statement that Gallaher replaced Karalis as the person cleared for entry.
subfiles.summary: Rawls says SCAP cleared D. M. Gallagher instead of Karalis, possibly because Pepsi-Cola changed representatives without notifying officials.

subfiles.title: Letter requesting return of Karalis’s permit
subfiles.from: Walter F. Chappell, Department of State
subfiles.about: Notifies Pepsi-Cola of the alleged substitution of Gallaher and asks for Karalis’s permit.
subfiles.summary: Chappell reports that the Army cancelled Karalis’s clearance in favor of Gallagher and requests the return of Karalis’s permit.

subfiles.title: Brazilian Embassy note renewing two Japan applications
subfiles.from: Embassy of Brazil
subfiles.about: Forwards corrected applications for Guilherme Meirelles and José de Abreu Lima.
subfiles.summary: The Embassy resubmits the businessmen’s applications after correcting the stated purpose of Meirelles’s travel.

subfiles.title: Application of Guilherme Meirelles
subfiles.from: Guilherme Meirelles
subfiles.about: Requests entry to Japan to study commerce and cereal imports.
subfiles.summary: Brazilian physician Guilherme Meirelles applies for a ten-day Tokyo visit to study cereal commerce and imports.

subfiles.title: Application of José de Abreu Lima
subfiles.from: José de Abreu Lima
subfiles.about: Requests entry to Japan with Meirelles to study the cereal trade.
subfiles.summary: Brazilian industrialist José de Abreu Lima applies to accompany Meirelles on a ten-day commercial study in Tokyo.

subfiles.title: Letter forwarding the Meirelles and Lima applications
subfiles.from: Walter F. Chappell, Division of Protective Services
subfiles.to: Lieutenant Colonel J. D. Scott, Military Permit Section
subfiles.about: Asks the Army to submit the renewed Brazilian applications to SCAP.
subfiles.summary: Chappell encloses both applications and requests their transmission to the Supreme Commander for a decision.

subfiles.title: Memorandum rejecting the Meirelles and Lima applications
subfiles.from: Department of State
subfiles.about: Reports occupation authorities’ refusal to admit the two men solely to study commercial possibilities.
subfiles.summary: State advises that Japan’s occupation authorities rejected the applications because current policy did not admit visitors merely to explore commerce and cereal imports were already arranged.

subfiles.title: Amalgamated Commercial Exporters letterhead sheet
subfiles.from: Amalgamated Commercial Exporters, Inc.
subfiles.about: Letterhead filed with Bassoon J. Fattal’s application materials.
subfiles.summary: Company letterhead and filing annotations accompany Fattal’s travel papers.

subfiles.title: Application of Bassoon J. Fattal to visit Japan
subfiles.from: Bassoon J. Fattal
subfiles.about: Requests business travel to Japan for textile exports and miscellaneous imports.
subfiles.summary: Iraqi exporter Bassoon J. Fattal describes his company, position, capitalization, and proposed Japanese textile trade.

subfiles.title: Letter enclosing Fattal’s military permit
subfiles.from: Walter F. Chappell, Department of State
subfiles.about: Sends military permit 9903 and requests departure details for an exit-permit waiver.
subfiles.summary: State sends Fattal his military permit and asks when and where he will leave the United States.

subfiles.title: Telephone memorandum concerning Ben S. Goldberg
subfiles.from: H. C. Corkran, Division of Protective Services
subfiles.about: Records Goldberg’s renewed wish to depart immediately and arrangements to return his permit to the Army.
subfiles.summary: Rawls says Goldberg again plans immediate travel; Corkran agrees to return the permit by courier.

subfiles.title: Letter returning Goldberg’s permit
subfiles.from: Walter F. Chappell, Division of Protective Services
subfiles.to: Lieutenant Colonel J. D. Scott, Military Permit Section
subfiles.about: Returns Ben S. Goldberg’s permit following the telephone conversation with Rawls.
subfiles.summary: Chappell returns Goldberg’s military permit and notes that State’s records have been updated.

subfiles.title: Transmittal slip to the Kobe Branch
subfiles.from: Walter F. Chappell, Division of Protective Services
subfiles.to: Kobe Branch, Office of the United States Political Adviser
subfiles.about: Transmits information concerning Naji Tacla and his family.
subfiles.summary: Internal slip forwards the Tacla matter to the Kobe Branch.

subfiles.title: Translation of Brazilian memorandum concerning Naji Tacla
subfiles.from: Embassy of Brazil
subfiles.about: Asks that Kobe officials inform Tacla that Brazilian visas can issue after legal requirements are met.
subfiles.summary: Brazil advises that its San Francisco consulate can grant temporary visas to Naji Tacla, his wife, and son.

subfiles.title: Portuguese original of Brazilian memorandum concerning Naji Tacla
subfiles.from: Embassy of Brazil
subfiles.about: Portuguese original of the request concerning visas for the Tacla family.
subfiles.summary: Original Portuguese note asks that Tacla’s family be advised about possible Brazilian temporary visas.

subfiles.title: Draft acknowledgment of the Brazilian Tacla memorandum
subfiles.from: Department of State
subfiles.about: Explains State’s interpretation of Brazil’s request and its inquiry into the family’s departure prospects.
subfiles.summary: State presumes Brazil wants Naji Tacla informed of visa eligibility, links him to earlier Nouri and Nagy Tacla correspondence, and requests a report from Japan before replying further.

subfiles.title: Instruction to the Yokohama Branch concerning Naji Tacla
subfiles.from: Secretary of State
subfiles.to: Officer in Charge, Yokohama Branch, Office of the United States Political Adviser
subfiles.about: Directs officials to inform Tacla and report whether his family can depart for Brazil.
subfiles.summary: The Yokohama Branch should notify Naji Tacla, investigate exit eligibility, and assist unless entry into the Western Hemisphere appears undesirable.

subfiles.title: Foreign Missions Conference request for two Finnish missionaries
subfiles.from: Royal H. Fisher, Foreign Missions Conference of North America
subfiles.about: Requests Japan entry permission for Miero and Lipponen under the revised missionary policy.
subfiles.summary: Fisher sponsors two Finnish women missionaries, supplies passport and travel details, guarantees their support, and notes their knowledge of Japanese.

subfiles.title: Yokohama airgram listing protecting powers
subfiles.from: Office of the United States Political Adviser, Yokohama
subfiles.about: Lists governments protecting the interests of countries without their own missions in Japan.
subfiles.summary: The airgram identifies protecting-power arrangements used by numerous countries in occupied Japan.

subfiles.title: SCAP announcement revising missionary entry procedures
subfiles.from: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
subfiles.about: Sets procedures for United States and non-United States missionaries seeking entry into Japan.
subfiles.summary: The announcement delegates clearance of American missionaries to State-supported mission boards while requiring other nationals to proceed through their governments or accredited protecting missions. It also distinguishes temporary visitors, returning missionaries, and applicants proposing new work.

subfiles.title: Reply to Fisher concerning Miero and Lipponen
subfiles.from: Walter F. Chappell, Division of Protective Services
subfiles.to: Royal H. Fisher, Foreign Missions Conference of North America
subfiles.about: Explains that the Finnish applicants must proceed through their protecting mission in Tokyo.
subfiles.summary: Because Miero and Lipponen are not U.S. citizens, Fisher is advised to have their sponsor in Japan approach the appropriate Swedish mission under SCAP policy.

subfiles.title: Incoming telegram from Yokohama
subfiles.from: Yokohama
subfiles.about: Incoming telegram filed under Japan entry matters; substantive text is illegible in the OCR.
subfiles.summary: Telegram forms identify Yokohama, but the message itself is not recoverable from the supplied OCR.

subfiles.title: Letter returning Victor B. Reuben’s permit
subfiles.from: Walter F. Chappell, Division of Protective Services
subfiles.to: Lieutenant Colonel J. D. Scott, Military Permit Section
subfiles.about: Returns Reuben’s permit because he cannot travel and plans to apply again later.
subfiles.summary: State returns the Iraqi businessman’s February 9 military permit to the Army for disposition.

subfiles.title: Telegram to Shanghai confirming Smirnoff and James clearances
subfiles.from: Department of State
subfiles.about: Confirms Japan entry permission for Ivan Smirnoff and Denis Corey James.
subfiles.summary: Shanghai is instructed to document the two company representatives’ clearance for a short March business visit to Japan.

subfiles.title: Telephone memorandum on Smirnoff’s delayed clearance notice
subfiles.from: H. C. Corkran, Division of Protective Services
subfiles.about: Records Standard Vacuum Oil’s request for an urgent follow-up cable to Shanghai.
subfiles.summary: After learning that the January airgram had not arrived, Corkran agrees to send a company-funded follow-up cable confirming Smirnoff’s clearance.

subfiles.title: Correction to the Finnish missionaries’ application details
subfiles.from: Royal H. Fisher, Foreign Missions Conference of North America
subfiles.about: Corrects wording in Fisher’s earlier letter concerning Miero, Lipponen, and Vihtori Volainen.
subfiles.summary: Fisher supplies corrections to names or wording in his February application letter.

subfiles.title: Syrian Industrial Trading follow-up on Japan application
subfiles.from: Syrian Industrial Trading Company
subfiles.about: Seeks acknowledgment and prompt action on a business-travel application and passport submitted February 4.
subfiles.summary: The applicant asks State to confirm favorable consideration so that travel arrangements can proceed.

subfiles.title: Incoming airgram record sheet
subfiles.about: Cover sheet for an incoming airgram whose substantive text is absent from the OCR.
subfiles.summary: Only the incoming-airgram form and filing stamps are legible.

subfiles.title: Visa Division memorandum concerning Heinrich Thore
subfiles.from: Visa Division, Department of State
subfiles.about: Recommends approaching the Army for expedited issuance of Thore’s Japan entry permit.
subfiles.summary: The Visa Division reports no security objection and suggests that Protective Services seek prompt Army action on Heinrich Thore’s permit.

subfiles.title: Egyptian Embassy note concerning Joseph Cassuto
subfiles.from: Royal Egyptian Embassy
subfiles.about: Requests permission for Joseph Cassuto to travel to Japan and Korea.
subfiles.summary: Embassy note underlying the Cassuto travel-permit correspondence.

subfiles.title: Memorandum for the files on handling Cassuto’s request
subfiles.from: Division of Protective Services
subfiles.about: Records advice that Egypt should use British channels, while Protective Services prepares a formal reply.
subfiles.summary: Jenkins told the Embassy that State could not transmit the request and recommended regular British channels.

subfiles.title: Receipt for Joseph Cassuto’s military permit
subfiles.from: Joseph Cassuto
subfiles.about: Acknowledges receipt of Army military permit 10241 for an April return journey to Japan.
subfiles.summary: Cassuto acknowledges receiving military permit 10241.

subfiles.title: Letter forwarding Cassuto’s application to the Army
subfiles.from: Walter F. Chappell, Division of Protective Services
subfiles.to: Lieutenant Colonel J. D. Scott, Military Permit Section
subfiles.about: Requests SCAP consideration of Cassuto’s application despite advising Egypt to use British channels in future.
subfiles.summary: State forwards Cassuto’s application as an exception and asks the Army to communicate SCAP’s decision.

subfiles.title: Reply to Egypt concerning Cassuto’s application
subfiles.from: Department of State
subfiles.about: Explains that Egyptian applications should be submitted through Britain as Egypt’s protecting power in Japan.
subfiles.summary: State recommends that Cassuto’s application proceed through regular British occupation channels.

subfiles.title: Pepsi-Cola letter disputing cancellation of Karalis’s clearance
subfiles.from: R. Van Horn, Pepsi-Cola Company
subfiles.about: Argues that Gallaher’s rather than Karalis’s clearance should have been cancelled.
subfiles.summary: Pepsi-Cola says Karalis already left for Japan with his permit, while Gallaher no longer worked for the company, suggesting an official mistake.

subfiles.title: Letter forwarding Antonio V. Rocha’s application
subfiles.from: Walter F. Chappell, Division of Protective Services
subfiles.to: Lieutenant Colonel J. D. Scott, Military Permit Section
subfiles.about: Transmits Manila’s request to validate Rocha’s Philippine passport for entry into Japan.
subfiles.summary: State asks the Army to obtain SCAP consideration for Sharpe and Company president Antonio V. Rocha’s Yokohama inspection trip.

subfiles.title: Plain telegram fragment concerning Rocha
subfiles.about: Fragmentary plain-language cable apparently clarifying Rocha’s name or application.
subfiles.summary: Only Rocha’s surname, a repeat instruction, and control markings remain legible.

subfiles.title: Army memorandum reporting Rocha’s theater clearance
subfiles.from: Military Permit Section, Department of the Army
subfiles.about: Reports theater action on Rocha’s entry as a company services representative.
subfiles.summary: The Army reports the theater’s entry decision for the representative identified in the preceding Rocha correspondence.

subfiles.title: Letter forwarding Pepsi-Cola’s correction to the Army
subfiles.from: Walter F. Chappell, Division of Protective Services
subfiles.to: Lieutenant Colonel J. D. Scott, Military Permit Section
subfiles.about: Forwards Van Horn’s account disputing the reported substitution of Gallaher for Karalis.
subfiles.summary: Chappell encloses Pepsi-Cola’s February 20 letter for investigation and any necessary correction of Army records.

subfiles.title: Argentine Embassy note transmitting Guerra’s application
subfiles.from: Embassy of the Argentine Republic
subfiles.about: Transmits Americo Guerra’s application for permission to enter Japan.
subfiles.summary: Argentine Embassy cover note for Guerra’s travel application.

subfiles.title: English application of Americo Guerra
subfiles.from: Americo Guerra
subfiles.about: Requests entry to Japan to investigate resumption of Argentine-Japanese commerce.
subfiles.summary: Argentine businessman Americo Guerra seeks a month-long Tokyo visit to study renewed commercial exchange with Japan.

subfiles.title: Spanish application and duplicate translation for Americo Guerra
subfiles.from: Americo Guerra and the Argentine Embassy
subfiles.about: Spanish-language application materials describing Guerra’s background, passport, itinerary, and commercial purpose.
subfiles.summary: The packet duplicates Guerra’s application in Spanish, identifying him as an Argentine commercial manager proposing to investigate postwar trade opportunities in Japan.

subfiles.title: Memorandum for the files on calls about Guerra
subfiles.from: H. C. Corkran, Division of Protective Services
subfiles.about: Records inquiries from a friend of Guerra and the Argentine ambassador about requested supporting information.
subfiles.summary: Corkran advises that Guerra should document prewar business connections with Japan to strengthen his application.

subfiles.title: Action slip requesting more information on Guerra
subfiles.from: Military Permit Section
subfiles.about: Indicates that additional information is required before action on Guerra’s application.
subfiles.summary: Entry-and-travel action slip requests further information.

subfiles.title: Letter forwarding Guerra’s application to the Army
subfiles.from: Walter F. Chappell, Division of Protective Services
subfiles.to: Lieutenant Colonel J. D. Scott, Military Permit Section
subfiles.about: Requests SCAP consideration of Guerra’s Argentine business-travel application.
subfiles.summary: Chappell encloses Guerra’s application and asks the Army to report the Supreme Commander’s decision.

subfiles.title: Memorandum to Argentina requesting more information on Guerra
subfiles.from: Department of State
subfiles.about: Reports that theater headquarters needs additional details about the purpose of Guerra’s trip.
subfiles.summary: State reviews transmission of Guerra’s application and asks the Embassy for further information before the case can return to SCAP.

subfiles.title: Incoming airgram record filed February 25
subfiles.about: Incoming-airgram record whose message text is absent from the OCR.
subfiles.summary: Only the communications form, file number, and filing stamps are legible.

subfiles.title: Memorandum for the files on protecting-power procedures
subfiles.from: Division of Protective Services
subfiles.about: Records debate over whether State should continue processing applications for countries represented by protecting powers.
subfiles.summary: Paige, Corkran, and Marx discuss softening a proposed circular, attaching a protecting-power list, and the danger that foreign governments might shift protection duties to the United States.

subfiles.title: Whitman memorandum on obtaining SCAP clearance
subfiles.from: Mr. Whitman, Office of Northeast Asian Affairs
subfiles.to: Mr. Williams, Division of Protective Services
subfiles.about: Recommends circular notes directing governments to seek SCAP clearance through their protecting powers.
subfiles.summary: Whitman explains SCAP’s interpretation of Circular 8 and proposes relieving U.S. diplomatic and Army channels of routine foreign applications.

subfiles.title: Routing sheet for protecting-power circular
subfiles.about: Internal routing sheet associated with the proposed circular note.
subfiles.summary: Largely blank routing form bearing Protective Services markings.

subfiles.title: Draft circular note on protecting-power applications
subfiles.from: Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Explains how governments without missions in Japan should use formally designated protecting powers for entry applications.
subfiles.summary: The draft reviews SCAP Circular 8 and states that applicants may be presented through a protecting power’s Tokyo mission. State will continue processing requests as a courtesy, but recommends the protecting-power route as faster and more appropriate; an attached table lists existing arrangements.

subfiles.title: Syrian Industrial Trading request for return of passport
subfiles.from: Syrian Industrial Trading Company
subfiles.about: Requests immediate return of a passport and suspension of the pending Japan business application.
subfiles.summary: Changed circumstances require the applicant’s passport, so the company asks State to hold the Japan application in abeyance.

subfiles.title: Army memorandum reporting theater clearance
subfiles.from: Military Permit Section, Department of the Army
subfiles.about: Reports receipt of theater action on an entry case, although the applicant’s name is illegible.
subfiles.summary: The Army advises State that theater clearance has been received; most identifying text is unreadable.
